_README: YOUR CARD VALUES. This is the trusted half of the pricing. Anything you list here is treated as truth and outranks whatever the tool infers from other eBay listings. Add cards you actually chase. Thirty to fifty is plenty to start, and you can add to it whenever you learn a new card.

_fields.year: Card year. For season-dated products like 2023-24, use the first year.
_fields.set: Lowercase, as the parser writes it: prizm, select, contenders, donruss optic, national treasures, immaculate, mosaic, topps chrome, spectra, origins, phoenix, absolute, flawless, zenith, certified, sp authentic
_fields.insert: The autograph subset, or null. Use: rookie auto, rookie ticket, rookie patch auto, rookie jersey auto, rated rookie, kaboom, draft picks
_fields.parallel: Colour or finish, or null for base. Use: silver, gold, green, blue, red, orange, holo, refractor, fire burst
_fields.player: Full name as printed on the card.
_fields.psa10Usd: What you believe it sells for in PSA 10, in US dollars. Your number.
_fields.serialOf: The print run denominator if numbered, e.g. 99 for /99. Otherwise null.
_fields.cardNo: Card number if you know it, otherwise null.
_fields.reviewed: Date you last checked this value. The tool warns when a value goes stale.

_note: Empty on purpose. This file used to ship six example rows with invented prices, and because your numbers outrank everything inferred, those inventions were being used as truth on every live scan. A wrong number here does more damage than no number at all. Fill it from data/my-values-TOFILL.json as you work out real values.
